The '''2012 [[Tippeligaen]]''' was the 68th completed season of top division [[association football|football]] in [[Norway]]. The competition began on 23 March 2012 and ended on 18 November 2012, with a summer break from 28 May to 30 June.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.vg.no/sport/fotball/norsk/artikkel.php?artid=10031259 |language=no |title=Eliteseriestart 25. mars neste år |publisher=[[Verdens Gang|VG]] |date=4 November 2011 |access-date=4 November 2011}}</ref> [[Molde FK|Molde]] were the defending champions,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.vg.no/sport/fotball/norsk/artikkel.php?artid=10023232 |language=no |title=Endelig tok sølvlaget Molde seriegull |work=vg.no |publisher=[[Verdens Gang|VG]] |date=30 October 2011 |access-date=20 November 2011}}</ref> while [[Hønefoss BK|Hønefoss]] and [[Sandnes Ulf]] entered as the promoted teams from the [[2011 1. divisjon]]. They replaced [[IK Start|Start]] and [[Sarpsborg 08 FF|Sarpsborg 08]] who were relegated to the [[2012 1. divisjon]]. 

On 11 November 2011, Molde won the title with one matchday left to play after a 1–0 home win over Hønefoss.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/international-football/2010/solskjaer-s-molde-champions-again-in-norway_sto3489101/story.shtml |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190507132203/https://www.eurosport.com/football/international-football/2010/solskjaer-s-molde-champions-again-in-norway_sto3489101/story.shtml |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 7, 2019 |title=Solskjaer's Molde champions again in Norway |website=[[Eurosport]] |agency=[[Reuters]] |date=11 November 2012 |access-date=7 May 2012}}</ref> It was their second consecutive league title and also their second top-flight title overall.

==Season summary==
{{expand section|date=November 2012}}
[[Strømsgodset Toppfotball|Strømsgodset]] were leading the league most of the season, but four matches before the end of the season there were three teams competing for the title. [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] lost out on the title-race after losing to Strømsgodset and [[Molde FK|Molde]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://fotball.adressa.no/eliteserien/article256336.ece |language=no |title=- Fortjent at Godset og Molde leder |publisher=Adresseavisen |date=4 November 2012 |access-date=20 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107121731/http://fotball.adressa.no/eliteserien/article256336.ece |archive-date=7 November 2012 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref> Molde secured the title in the 29th round after they won 1&ndash;0 at home, while Strømsgodset lost 2&ndash;1 against Sandnes Ulf.

[[Stabæk Fotball|Stabæk]] were relegated after being positioned at the bottom of the table throughout the season. Ahead of the last round, four teams were fighting against relegation, but [[Fredrikstad FK|Fredrikstad]] lost their match against the league-winners Molde and were relegated, while [[Sandnes Ulf]] finished 14th and played relegation play-offs against [[Ullensaker/Kisa IL|Ullensaker/Kisa]], the sixth-placed team in the [[2012 1. divisjon|1. divisjon]]. Sandnes Ulf won the play-offs 7–1 on aggregate (4–0 away and 3–1 at home), and were not relegated.

The average attendance in 2012 were 7,014 spectators, down from 7,995 in 2011, which was the lowest average attendance in Tippeligaen since 2003.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://fotball.aftenposten.no/eliteserien/article257996.ece |language=no |title=Laveste tilskuersnitt på ni år |publisher=Aftenposten |work=Norwegian News Agency |date=20 November 2012 |access-date=20 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121124111926/http://fotball.aftenposten.no/eliteserien/article257996.ece |archive-date=24 November 2012 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

==Teams==
Sixteen teams competed in the league – the top fourteen teams from the previous season and the two teams promoted from the [[2011 1. divisjon|1. divisjon]] The promoted teams were [[Hønefoss BK|Hønefoss]] (returning after a season's absence) and [[Sandnes Ulf]] (their first post-[[World War II]] top-flight season). They replaced [[Sarpsborg 08 FF|Sarpsborg 08]] (relegated after their first ever presence) and [[IK Start|Start]] (ending their three-year spell in the top flight).

==Relegation play-offs==
{{main|2012 Eliteserien promotion/relegation play-offs}}
At the end of the season, [[Stabæk Fotball|Stabæk]] and [[Fredrikstad FK|Fredrikstad]] were relegated directly to 1. divisjon, and will be replaced by [[IK Start|Start]] and [[Sarpsborg 08 FF|Sarpsborg]] who were directly promoted.

Five teams entered a play-off for the last Tippeligaen spot in the 2013 season. These were:
* A) [[Sandnes Ulf]] (by virtue of being the 14th placed team in the Tippeligaen)
* B) [[Sandefjord Fotball|Sandefjord]] (by virtue of being the third placed team in the 1. divisjon)
* C) [[Mjøndalen IF|Mjøndalen]] (by virtue of being the fourth placed team in the 1. divisjon)
* D) [[FK Bodø/Glimt|Bodø/Glimt]] (by virtue of being the fifth placed team in the 1. divisjon)
* E) [[Ullensaker/Kisa IL|Ullensaker/Kisa]] (by virtue of being the sixth placed team in the 1. divisjon)

The four 1. divisjon teams first played a single game knockout tournament, with the winner (Ull/Kisa) advancing to a two-legged tie against the Tippeligaen team (Sandnes Ulf) for the 16th and final spot in the 2013 season. Sandnes Ulf retained their Tippeligaen spot with an aggregate 7–1 win over Ull/Kisa.
